purpose: Fail-closed declaration consumed by the proposed P1-A patch to tools/audit_26_closure_readiness.py. It enumerates the wrapper identities that historical #26 evidence is allowed to pin while the canonical repository path has moved on. Any wrapper digest not listed here must still be treated by the auditor as drift.
rule: A listed identity is accepted ONLY when its bytes are re-hashed from the declared archived_repo_path and match both sha256 and size_bytes. If the archived copy is missing, untracked, a symlink or a reparse point, the identity is rejected and the audit must fail.

identities.archived_copy_uniqueness: This is the only tracked model.cpp in the repository whose bytes hash to this digest at the time of adjudication. Further untracked copies exist under validation/** run trees but are not durable.
identities.why_not_a_git_object: The 1864 B bytes were an uncommitted working-tree variant at build time. Commit 55773c5 committed a different 1864 B blob (e0e96466a407d49572a8f3ec911515b4e855147f), so this digest was never committed at the canonical path and can never be produced by git from history.
identities.retention_authority: docs/plan/26-current-wrapper-recheck-plan.md:103 forbids writing new evidence into the historical directories or the closure manifest; :145-152 marks those paths read-only and byte-unchanged.
unverified_surface_remaining: same-source terrain input (wk_model_step_with_terrain) is implemented but not driven by any probe

acceptance_effect.note: This declaration resolves only the provenance-binding classification. It does not close #26, does not accept the unverified interfaces, and does not change any closure blocker.
